output_list.reason: The mintlvlToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initial supply is set to the owner, but there is no check to prevent overflow during minting additional tokens. This can be exploited to increase the balance of any user, allowing attackers to achieve a denial of service attack.

The burnlvlToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initial supply is set to the owner, but there is no check to prevent overflow during burning tokens. This can be exploited to decrease the balance of any user, allowing attackers to achieve a denial of service attack.

The lend function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The function does not check if the total supply is exceeded when a user lends tokens, allowing attackers to overflow the total supply, achieving a denial of service attack.

The repayLoan function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The function does not check if the total supply is exceeded when a user repays tokens, allowing attackers to overflow the total supply, achieving a denial of service attack.
The setlvlSign function allows the owner to set a new sign, but it does not verify the length of the input, allowing attackers to overflow the input, achieving a wrong logic attack.
